| `SEC-KEY-001` | P0 | Verifying services hold public material only. The property is now per-service rather than global: the auth service IS an issuer and must hold its own key at 0400, while every other running container holds none and the bootstrap issuer's key stays in the root plane. The key set is compared in four readings -- the deployed document, what the issuer publishes, what the deploy wrote, and the bytes inside the PostgREST container -- because a JWKS replaced at a stable path leaves a running verifier holding the old inode (D278). | `tests/deployment/test_session6_tokens.py::test_no_verifier_holds_private_signing_material`<br>`tests/deployment/test_session6_tokens.py::test_the_published_key_set_is_what_every_verifier_actually_loaded` |
| `SEC-KEY-002` | P0 | Prepare, acknowledge, promote, retire: promotion is blocked until every verifier has acknowledged the prepared public generation, and retirement may not run before the deadline. The transition itself is NOT exercised in Session 6 and that is a decision (ADR 0088): the transition is the first rotation the machinery exists for, and Session 6 builds the machinery rather than driving it. What the live proofs assert is everything that holds without starting one -- the deployed key state satisfies the model's own validator, no rotation is in flight, the acknowledgement record is null rather than empty, and the published set holds exactly the key that signs. That last one replaced a two-key assertion when ADR 0170 retired the bootstrap issuer: until Session 15 two live issuers filled the two-key ceiling, which was the reason no rotation could be prepared at all (D683). The slot is now free, so the ceiling is no longer the reason -- the scope of Session 6 is. Retire has a THIRD outcome since ADR 0224 and it is reported rather than refused: one published kid, no deadline and no acknowledgement is a state a deploy has already retired, and the refusal that used to fire there said the opposite of the truth to an operator who had just completed a rotation (D1580). A run is enqueued as the token's agent, authorised by the agent's STORED scopes: `scope_not_held` is a 403 carrying the substrate's word, and a revoked agent is a 401, not a 403. A definition nobody installed, a run that does not exist and another agent's run are ONE 404, `no_such_workflow`, so no answer is an existence oracle. | `WF-WORK-001` | P0 | **The loop inside the auth process** (ADR 0226). It claims, mints, calls and finishes in that order; one token per step attempt, minted through `step_token` -- the status and expiry checks an agent's own mint passes, minus the secret -- and dropped on every path out of the step. The call carries the step's derived key and the agent's token and **no request id** (D1696): the plane mints its own and ignores a caller's, so the loop reads the RESPONSE's and records it on finish and park, and `None` where no call was made or the header is not a uuid. A successful call finishes `succeeded` -- a replay is indistinguishable in the plane's result and the loop never guesses one (D1671); a tool refusal is an HTTP 200 with `result.isError`, read FIRST (D1672); `write_conflict`, a transport error and a 5xx park with the declared backoff while attempts remain and then fail naming the token; any other refusal fails the run naming it; a 401 or 403 from the plane, or a refused mint, stops the run as `agent_not_active` with no call. A dry run marks writes and leaves reads alone. The lease margin is a FUNCTION of the plane client's one timeout (D1670) and the loop stops before its lease does. An exception is logged and the loop re-entered without stopping the verifier; the heartbeat is written each poll; the loop starts in `auth` mode only, reads no variable that mode did not already read, names no banned transport and addresses the plane by three constants bound to the deploy's own (D1685). | ## Requirement ID prefixes

| Prefix | Area |
|---|---|
| `DEP` | Deployment, bootstrap, and project isolation |
| `CFG` | Manifests, naming, rendering, and generated configuration |
| `DBX` | Database endpoints and client compatibility |
| `SEC` | Authorization, credentials, and security boundaries |
| `API` | PostgREST and FastAPI contracts |
| `AGT` | MCP and agent behavior |
| `STO` | Object storage |
| `REC` | Backup and recovery |
| `OPS` | Health, diagnostics, logging, and operations |
| `DX` | Developer experience and documentation |
